rules.text: Classify minor surface creases, wrinkles, or slight scuffs on flexible packaging as normal unless they compromise structural integrity or legibility.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged natural handling artifacts (wrinkles, scuffs) on a flexible bag as anomalies. This rule explicitly tolerates these common, non-defective features to prevent false positives.

rules.text: Classify surface wrinkles, creases, and minor seal folds on flexible food packaging as normal manufacturing or handling artifacts.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged natural packaging wrinkles and creases as defects. This rule explicitly defines these common physical characteristics as normal, preventing false positives on flexible items.

rules.text: Flag packages where the transparent window is obscured by dark, irregular, or non-uniform contents that deviate from the standard product appearance.
rules.justification: The agent dismissed the anomaly because the logo was intact. This rule forces inspection of the product visibility through the window, catching the dark, irregular contents that constitute the actual defect.

rules.text: Treat minor wrinkling at package seals and slight creases on edges as normal handling variations, not defects.
rules.justification: The agent flagged natural handling artifacts (wrinkles, creases) as potential defects. This rule explicitly categorizes these common features as normal, preventing false positives.

rules.text: Do not classify a box as crushed if the deformation is limited to minor edge warping or slight corner compression without structural collapse.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged minor edge warping as severe crushing. This rule clarifies that slight deformations are acceptable normal variations, preventing false positives on structurally intact boxes.

rules.text: Treat specular highlights and glare on glossy packaging surfaces as normal lighting artifacts, not defects.
rules.justification: The agent flagged a reflection on the glossy box as a potential anomaly. This rule explicitly categorizes such lighting effects as normal, preventing false positives on shiny surfaces.

rules.text: Treat upright food boxes with standard vertical text and clear branding as normal, even if the image is cropped or the box is narrow.
rules.justification: The agent likely flagged the narrow, cropped view of the standard product packaging as anomalous. This rule clarifies that such framing does not constitute a defect for this class.

rules.text: Classify as anomaly if the box top flap exhibits a large, irregular hole or physical tear.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the hole but failed to maintain the high anomaly score. This rule explicitly defines flap damage as a definitive anomaly, preventing future refutation of such clear defects.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if the can body exhibits significant vertical wrinkling, buckling, or deformation, even if the label print remains intact.
rules.justification: The agent missed the severe structural deformation (buckling) on the can's side, focusing only on print quality. This rule explicitly targets physical shape defects.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if the carton lacks an attached straw, as this is a required feature for the class.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly refuted the anomaly due to a false positive detection of a straw. This rule explicitly defines the absence of a straw as the anomaly condition, correcting the logic.

rules.text: Do not flag minor surface smudges or dust on labels as defects if the underlying text and graphics remain clear and legible.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged a minor smudge as a defect. This rule clarifies that superficial imperfections do not constitute anomalies when the label's informational content is intact.

rules.text: If a transparent straw wrapper is attached to the front of the carton, classify as anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the wrapper but failed to confirm it. This rule explicitly defines the attached wrapper as a defect, ensuring the anomaly is correctly identified.

rules.text: Do not flag items as anomalies solely due to different flavor variants or seasonal packaging designs if the core brand identity and product structure remain consistent.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly identified a standard flavor variant (blueberry) as an anomaly because its design differed from the reference set. This rule clarifies that design variations for different flavors are normal.

rules.text: Classify as anomaly if the cigarette pack flap is torn, frayed, or physically damaged, regardless of face orientation.
rules.justification: The agent missed the physical damage on the top flap, incorrectly assuming the back view was sufficient for a normal classification. This rule explicitly flags structural defects.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if the pack face features a large diagonal stripe or landscape graphic instead of the standard solid background with leaf logo.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the design mismatch but was uncertain. This rule explicitly defines the specific visual deviation (diagonal stripe/landscape) as a definitive anomaly, preventing future hesitation on similar design variations.

rules.text: Classify cigarette packs with open top flaps or exposed inner packaging as anomalies.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the open flap but lowered the score. This rule explicitly defines the open state as an anomaly, ensuring high confidence for this defect type.

rules.text: Do not flag label rotation or slight misalignment as an anomaly if the bottle is not perfectly front-facing.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged the label's apparent rotation as a defect. This rule clarifies that such visual shifts are normal artifacts of the bottle's orientation, not physical damage.

rules.text: If a drink bottle lacks a visible label or branding on its main body, classify it as an anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the missing label but lowered the score. This rule reinforces that the absence of a label is a definitive anomaly for this class, preventing uncertainty.

rules.text: Do not flag minor foil lid tears or crinkles as anomalies if they are consistent with standard packaging variations seen in reference images.
rules.justification: The agent initially flagged a lid tear as a defect (score 0.65). The rule clarifies that such minor packaging imperfections are normal variations, preventing false positives when reference images show similar features.

rules.text: Treat any small, irregular white mark or scuff on the printed label surface as a defect, even if the mark is tiny.
rules.justification: The agent initially flagged the mark but then refuted it. This rule reinforces that small surface imperfections on labels are valid anomalies, preventing the agent from dismissing them as noise.
